title: Investigation templates: latency story and trace slimming
content:
Purpose:
This doc provides compact, reusable investigation templates for latency incidents and a prescriptive 'trace slimming' workflow operators and SREs can apply to keep trace cost low while preserving signal needed for root-cause. It also outlines a lightweight dashboard subscription lifecycle (creation -> TTL -> archival) so we avoid dashboard sprawl.

Scope:
- Low-to-medium severity latency anomalies for inference pipelines (prefix/kvcache, tokenization, model execution).
- Applies to hosted, dedicated, and private deployments.
- Intended for oncall and engineers running postmortems and short runbook investigations.

1) Latency story template (copyable)
- Title: [short human title: e.g., "Model-2 cold K/V warm-up spike 2026-01-05"]
- Symptom: [what users/operators observed; e.g., 95th token latency rose from 220ms -> 680ms across region-us-west1]
- Impacted cohort: [tenant subset, routes, model versions, time window]
- SLI/metric anchors: [primary SLI name and exact query; e.g., inference.token.latency_p95(route=\"generate\", model=\"m-3b\") over 5m window]
- Baseline and delta: [normal vs observed quantiles and token counts]
- First five diagnostic checks (ordered):
  1. Check recent deploys/rollouts (A/B, canary) for model or runtime config. Link to rollout id.
  2. Verify node CPU/GPU saturation and host-level queuing (top-kvm, io, dmesg).
  3. Confirm KV cache hit ratios and prefix-warmth (kv.prefetch_hit_rate by tenant).
  4. Sample 10 request traces (see trace anchor below) to identify slow spans.
  5. Check autoscaler events / scaling cooldown for spikes.
- Probable root causes (to consider): cold KV cache, slow model kernel path (quantized fallback), noisy tenant, network jitter to storage, GC pauses in sidecars.
- Mitigation checklist: roll back to previous model variant, enable temporary routing to dedicated pool, increase probe cadence for KV warming, raise sampling for affected tenant.

Trace anchor & sampling keys (how to pick traces)
- Anchor spans to include: request.start -> tokenizer -> model.exec -> kv.lookup -> model.postproc.
- Create a temporary high-fidelity sampling policy: sample 100% for requests matching route+model for 15 minutes, otherwise 1% global. Annotate with investigation id.

2) Trace slimming sequences (step-by-step)
Goal: preserve diagnostic signal while bounding trace volume and cost.
Sequence:
- Step A: Identify investigation tag (INV-####) and annotate incoming traffic via header/tag.
- Step B: Create a time-bounded sampling policy:
  - Phase 1 (diagnose, 0-15m): 100% for affected cohort, 2% for others.
  - Phase 2 (narrow, 15-90m): sample heuristically (all traces with error/latency>p90 OR traces with heavy kv miss) plus 0.5% baseline.
  - Phase 3 (cleanup): revert to steady-state sampling and persist condensed trace anchors for 7d.
- Step C: Apply span-level slimming rules in the trace pipeline (examples):
  - Drop verbose middleware spans (health-check, metrics emit) unless error=true.
  - Truncate large attribute blobs (user prompt) and replace with hash + length metadata.
  - Coalesce repetitive microspans into a single synthetic span (e.g., batch shard loops).
- Step D: Export condensed traces to long-term storage only for traces with a 'root_cause_likelihood' tag > 0.6.

Sampling budget quick formula:
- budget_traces_per_min = max(5, floor(0.01 * requests_per_min))
- aim to keep additional traced tokens under quota Q (operator-estimated). If bursting, apply adaptive backoff: reduce sampling by factor 2 when trace-ingest-Q > 80%.

3) Dashboard subscription lifecycle (short policy)
- Create: new dashboard requires an owner, a one-line purpose, and linked alert(s). Add TTL field at creation.
- Active period: 0-90 days (default 30d). If still used (view count > 10/week or linked to active alert), auto-extend to 180d.
- Review: at TTL expiry, owner receives a review prompt. Options: extend, archive to gallery, or delete.
- Archival: archived dashboards move to `/dashboards/archives` and show a short summary + last-used metric snapshot.
- Naming convention: <team>-<purpose>-<last-action-month> (e.g., obs-kv-warmth-Jan2026)

4) Investigation priority rubric (quick)
Score = 3*user_impact + 2*latency_delta_score + 1*regression_risk
- user_impact: 0 (no users) | 1 (small cohort) | 2 (multiple customers) | 3 (broad outage)
- latency_delta_score: 0 (<10% change) | 1 (10-30%) | 2 (30-100%) | 3 (>100%)
- regression_risk: 0 (no recent change) | 1 (recent canary) | 2 (config change) | 3 (model rollout)
Interpretation: >=8 urgent paging, 5-7 triage, <=4 backlog work.

5) Quick-check checklist for oncall (copy into slack)
- Is there an active rollout? (Y/N)
- Are autoscaler events correlated?
- KV hit rate changed? (Y/N + delta)
- Top 3 slow traces preserved? (link)
- Mitigation applied? (what & when)

6) Postmortem evidence to collect
- time-sliced latency quantiles, traffic shards, top-ten trace summaries (condensed), node-level CPU/GPU metrics, autoscaler logs, rollout ids, and probe histories.

7) Notes on instrumentation hygiene (mini-guidelines)
- Use stable metric names (avoid ad-hoc suffixes).
- Emit tenant and route tags on all latency metrics for sliceability.
- Prefer lightweight boolean tags (cache_hit=true) over verbose text fields to preserve cardinality budgets.
- Add an "investigation_id" tag to metrics and spans when running high-fidelity captures; make it easy to query across stores.

8) Template snippets (example queries)
- p95 delta query text (promql-style):
  increase(inference_token_requests_total{route=\"chat\"}[5m]) > 0 and
  (histogram_quantile(0.95, sum(rate(inference_token_duration_seconds_bucket[5m])) by (le, route, model)) - baseline_p95) 

9) Follow-ups and ownership
- Owner: [name] must close investigation with a 1-paragraph summary, a list of evidence, and recommended infra/product actions.
- Archive traces and dashboards used in investigation under the investigation id.

Appendix: small heuristics cheat-sheet for trace slimming rules and span priorities (copy into runbooks).

-- End of doc --
